definitions.explanation: A boundary or endpoint. Almost always used in the negative pattern 際限がない or 際限なく to mean "without limit" or "endlessly."

examples.japanese: {欲望|よくぼう}には{際限|さいげん}がない。
{際限|さいげん}なく{食|た}べ{続|つづ}けてしまう。
この{議論|ぎろん}は{際限|さいげん}がないから、そろそろ{結論|けつろん}を{出|だ}しましょう。
examples.english: This debate has no end, so let's reach a conclusion soon.

notes:
Compound of {際|さい} (edge/boundary) + {限|げん} (limit). Overwhelmingly used in the negative.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {際限|さいげん}がない (there is no limit; limitless)
- {際限|さいげん}なく (without limit; endlessly)
- {際限|さいげん}のない (limitless; unbounded)

USAGE NOTE:
Rarely if ever used in the affirmative. You would not normally say {際限|さいげん}がある. Instead, this word's function is almost entirely as part of the negative pattern expressing limitlessness. Similar to how the English word "cessation" mainly appears in the phrase "without cessation."
